events.content: CoreWeave top customer concentration percentage revenue 2026

**CoreWeave remains highly concentrated in Microsoft, not OpenAI, on recognized revenue.** Microsoft accounted for approximately **67% of FY2025 revenue** ($5.131 billion), or roughly **$3.44 billion**, versus 62% in FY2024 and 35% in FY2023. [[1]] 

OpenAI was **not a ≥10% revenue customer in FY2025**: CoreWeave disclosed that no customer other than Microsoft represented 10% or more of FY2025 revenue. [[1]] 

That said, OpenAI is an exceptionally material **forward backlog/customer-credit exposure** rather than a disclosed current-revenue concentration. Its initial March 2025 agreement committed OpenAI to pay up to approximately **$11.9 billion through October 2030**, and a September 2025 order form added up to approximately **$6.5 billion through May 2031**; CoreWeave explicitly said it expected OpenAI to become a significant future customer. [[2]] 

CoreWeave subsequently described total OpenAI contract value at approximately **$22.4 billion**, including the initial agreement, a May 2025 expansion, and the September expansion. [[3]]

**Bottom line:** Microsoft is the dominant near-term P&L concentration risk—two-thirds of FY2025 sales—while OpenAI is the major medium-term concentration and counterparty risk embedded in contracted backlog and planned capacity deployment. [[4]] [[2]]

Sources:
[S3.1] CoreWeave revenue surges to $5.1B on AI cloud boom — https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CRWV/10-k-core-weave-inc-files-annual-report-765643168fc2.html

tool_arguments.summary:
CoreWeave's financial metrics as of its most recently reported periods (Q2 FY2026 ended June 30, 2026):
- Revenue: $2.575 billion for Q2 FY2026, up from $1.212 billion in Q2 FY2025 (S1.1).
- Contracted backlog: approximately $104 billion as of June 30, 2026 (S2.1).
- Customer concentration: Microsoft accounted for ~67% of FY2025 revenue (~$3.44 billion of $5.131 billion), with no other customer reaching 10% of FY2025 revenue (S3.1–S3.4).
- Recent acquisition: Completed the purchase of AI-development-platform Weights & Biases for roughly $1.7 billion, finalized May 5, 2025 (S5.1, S5.3, S5.4). A proposed all-stock acquisition of Core Scientific implied ~$9.0 billion equity value but was terminated after shareholder opposition (S5.5, S5.6).
All figures are cited to their primary source documents.
